b) A service ( ⁧تقرير⁩ ) with a personal case. Start with a scene and a person (Rīm) to make concrete the theme before the data. About one third of the medical graduates left in five years; rural hospitals have a serious shortage of staff. It increased the salaries of 15% incentives to work in campaigns are launched; the union president responds that the problem is not only salary, but working conditions and recognition. Living away from home is difficult, but waiting here is harder. ⁧الغربة⁩ is the personal experience, often painful, of living away from one's own land; ⁧الاغتراب⁩ is the most general (also sociological) term for emigration and, in other contexts, alienation.

Exercise 10 · Example. "We love our country... but we want to live": young doctors pack bags. In the waiting room of a language school in the capital, Rīm, 27-year-old doctor, is sitting in front of a German manual. "I work sixty hours a week and my salary isn't enough to pay the rent," he calmly says. "I don't want to leave, but I don't see a future here." Rīm is one of the thousands of young doctors preparing to emigrate. According to the Order of Doctors of the Republic of the Sea, in five years he has left the country about one third of the new graduates, while rural hospitals suffer from a serious shortage of personnel. The Ministry of Health claims to have increased the salaries of 15% and have launched an incentive programme for those working in rural areas. But for the president of the Order, "the problem is not just salary, it is working conditions and recognition." As for RīmHe says he'll come back "one day, if anything changes." And he adds, smiling: "Living away from home is difficult, but staying here waiting is harder." ⁧الغربة⁩ does not have a unique equivalent; "Live far from home" means "exile" (too strong) or "emigration" (too neutral): the chosen yield retains the contrast of the phrase.
